problem: Disney wanted a stronger animation pipeline and a better relationship with Pixar's leadership.
title: Disney acquires Pixar in an all-stock deal valued at $7.4 billion
context: Disney and Pixar had a distribution relationship and talks on extending it had stalled.
decision_made: Acquire Pixar for about $7.4 billion in stock, making Steve Jobs Disney's largest shareholder.
action_taken: Left the two studios separate, kept Pixar in Emeryville and gave John Lasseter a senior creative role.
observed_outcome: Not documented in the sources used. Disney said at the time the deal would lower earnings for two years and add to earnings by 2008.
lessons: Acquirers sometimes buy relationships and talent as much as assets, and say upfront when payback will come.
limitations: Only the announcement and projections were checked here. Sources differ on Lasseter's title.

claims.claim_text: Disney agreed to buy Pixar in an all-stock deal valued at $7.4 billion.
Disney said the deal would lower earnings for two years and add to them by 2008.
